sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q1–Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Vantage sector intel, 20 Nov 2026
title: US orders came back. Not every exporter got them.
dek: Textile exporters grew revenue a median 22% as US orders delayed by the 50% duty returned: Kitex, Indo Count and Pearl Global grew 37–66%, but Himatsingka and Trident shrank.

read: The US order recovery is real but uneven; watch whether exporters hold margins after the festive mix and whether UK and EU enquiries become orders.
notes: Export-led home-textile and garment makers that filed Q2 FY27 results (consolidated), sorted by revenue growth; margin is operating (EBITDA) margin vs Q2 FY26. Indo Count's filed margin is 13.9% (9.8%), below the 15.3% EBITDA margin stated on its call, which uses a different definition. Kitex's margin jump (+35 pt) is off a loss-making year-ago quarter, and Trident also sells yarn and paper. S.P. Apparels and Vardhman had no filed results on the desk. The earlier Byte 'Textile makers widened margins' covered yarn and fabric makers; this one looks only at exporters.
